0.15.475 Nov 23, 2026

0.15.474 Nov 23, 2026
- Free build: every Free build area now has an owner of its own, the way a flame altar's area does (your own area: you; each remembered spot: a number of its own from the game). Without one, the game took the areas for changed every moment and reloaded the ground under them, which slowed servers down.

If EMF's loader itself was removed, FlameKit cannot start and cannot do this.

A kill by your companion or pet counts as yours. - Test monsters: the dummy no longer swings at you; it just stands there. Anyone can still hit it.
- Messages: switching an experimental option is announced as "Ninechars turned ON no shroud damage." (or OFF), and these lines (PvP joined/left too) also show for about 10 seconds in orange in everyone's Notices window.
- Windows tab (F4): the minimap has its row there now, with Show/Hide and "Reset place" (the Minimap tab's Location section is gone; Shape is under Size). New "Reset All" puts every window back at its default place and size.

0.15.138 Nov 14, 2026
- Messages: when the server is updated while you play, it says "Server updated to FlameKit vX."
- Messages: a clear warning when your game and the server's FlameKit are too far apart to work together (and what to do). A server that is a little older but still works with your game no longer gets an orange warning.

0.15.137 Nov 14, 2026
- Server: spawning a lot of test monsters no longer stops FlameKit on the server (it did with 100: the Party list and everything else stopped until a restart). Big spawns now come 20 at a time, and every scan over the world is kept short.
- Test monsters no longer protect pets, animals or buildings near them: they are monsters. Spawn them away from bases.
- If you leave the server while your monsters are still being spawned, the rest are not made.

0.15.136 Nov 14, 2026
- PvP: the kill notice is red now and stays up for 2 minutes.
- PvP: if you die with PvP on, you are out of PvP until you switch it on again (free-for-all).
- PvP: the cool-down is only started again by damage from another PvP player, not by heals, buffs or regeneration.
- Test monsters: "Quantity" (was "How many") is 1, 15, 50, 100 or 200. The level is picked with its five buttons (the < > is gone).
- Test monsters: Remove now removes all your test monsters wherever they are, and any left behind with nobody to remove them.

0.15.135 Nov 14, 2026

0.15.134 Nov 14, 2026

- PvP: once another PvP player hits you, you cannot switch PvP off for a minute. The Party list shows everyone how long is left ("PvP 42s").
- Test monsters: anyone can hit and kill the dummy now, PvP on or off. It still never hurts anyone.
- Test monsters: "How many" spawns up to 5 duelists at once, side by side.

The leaderboard no longer uses the account name of the player who died, and nearby players on the minimap keep their account names on a server without FlameKit.

0.15.69 Nov 14, 2026
- PvP: with several PvP players near a monster, every one of them is now in its threat table, and the game itself chooses whom it fights (by aggro: who hits it, how hard, how close), the same way it does with normal players. Before, one of them was picked at random and forced as its target.

0.15.68 Nov 14, 2026
- PvP: monsters now really fight a player with PvP on (tested with the duelist: it attacks within a second). The game's own threat event was not enough: each monster within 20 m of a PvP player also gets that player as its target and in its threat table, the way the game keeps a normal player there.
- PvP test bodies: a body spawned right after a long move is no longer lost track of.

0.15.67 Nov 14, 2026
- PvP: monsters ignored a player with PvP on (the game's monsters only pick players as targets, and a PvP player no longer counts as one). Now every monster within 20 m of a PvP player is pointed at them every 2 seconds with the game's own threat event, so PvP never makes you safe from monsters.

0.15.66 Nov 14, 2026
- PvP test bodies, to try PvP alone (Experimental, Debug section): "Spawn PvP dummy" puts a player-like body 3 m in front of you. With PvP on it swings at you but does no damage; hit it to see whether your weapons hurt a player. "Spawn PvP duelist" puts a Vukah fighter there that attacks everyone with full damage, PvP on or off. It never hurts animals, pets or buildings; villagers are fair game. "Remove" takes your body away. One at a time; it is gone after a reload or when you leave.

0.15.65 Nov 14, 2026
- New in Experimental: "PvP (free-for-all)". Players who switch it on can hurt each other with their normal weapons, arrows and spells, at 25% of the damage. Players without it cannot hurt them or be hurt by them. Everyone on the server is told who switched it on. It goes off again when you leave the server. Careful: while it is on, your hits can also hurt your own summons, pets and villagers. Not yet tried with two players.

0.15.57 Nov 13, 2026

- Auto Junk List: on joining a server, your junk list no longer goes missing for about 2 minutes. The first message after joining was often lost (the link to the server drops messages while the game is still loading); now the server confirms each list and your game sends it again every 5 seconds until it does (6 times at most).

- New Notices window: warnings that stay on screen until they are solved, instead of scrolling away in Messages. It has no title bar; hold the pointer key to drag it anywhere or size it at its lower right corner. It shows only while there is a notice (and not in the game's menus); FlameKit's window, tab Windows, can reset its place.
- Auto Junk List: the "Auto-Collect Scattered Loot" warning moved from Messages to the Notices window. It is there for as long as junk is set to Drop while that game option is on, and goes away by itself once you turn the option off or set Delete.
- Party window: the buff and debuff badges are bigger (30 px) and show the time left inside the icon (seconds under a minute, then minutes, then hours). A player with buffs takes 10 px more room than one without.

0.15.53 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: when you turn "Auto-Collect Scattered Loot" off in the game, its red warnings leave the Messages window by themselves (within a second or so).

0.15.52 Nov 13, 2026
- Party window: the buffs and debuffs moved onto the name line, behind each player's name, as small badges (debuffs first), so a player takes no more room than before. When more are active than fit, the last badge says "+3" and lists the rest when you point at it. The time left is in the tooltip; a buff with less than 10 s left is drawn fainter.

0.15.51 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: the red message about "Auto-Collect Scattered Loot" no longer says "(drop failed)".

0.15.50 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: the warning is back in FlameKit's window. While junk is set to Drop and the game's "Auto-Collect Scattered Loot" is on, a red line over your bag says so (it was lost with the old panel in 0.15.49's cleanup). The red message in Messages when junk is dropped stays as it was.

0.15.49 Nov 13, 2026
- Party window: every player's buffs and debuffs, with the game's own icons: a badge per buff (green buff, red debuff, amber food, blue rested, brown terrain) and the time left under it. Debuffs come first. Hold the pointer key and point at a badge for its name and the exact time left. Everyone in the game sees everyone's buffs. Test players have some too.
- Auto Junk List: Dump Junk in FlameKit's window now works in a world you host yourself (single player or hosting); before, it only worked on a server.
- Privacy: the server's log no longer names players by their account number (it could be shared with a bug report); it uses their number in the game instead.
- After a game update FlameKit no longer reads the places in the game's memory it found on the current game version (map markers, names, quest marks, item details) until a FlameKit version knows the new one: nothing wrong is read.
- FlameKit Native says in its mod.json that it is only needed in a player's game, not on a server (EMF.exe shows that to server owners).
- Cleanup: the old Auto Junk List panel (from the EMF window) and its icon files are gone; FlameKit's window does all of it.

0.15.48 Nov 13, 2026
- Party window and minimap: the server now knows who is playing from EMF's own join and leave reports, instead of guessing the first 64 player numbers. A player is never missed, however many have come and gone.

0.15.47 Nov 13, 2026
- Updates: after a failed or refused update, the message at the bottom left goes away once a later check finds everything in order.

0.15.46 Nov 13, 2026
- Test release: the DLL is rebuilt with no feature change, to check that a second update in one game session replaces the first one that is still waiting.

0.15.45 Nov 13, 2026
- Updates are signed: FlameKit only installs an update that carries the signature of FlameKit's release key, which never leaves the developer's PC. A change to the update files on GitHub alone can no longer reach your game.
- On a server with an older FlameKit than yours, an orange line under the FlameKit label says so (and that some features are off).
- Cleanup: leftovers of the old panel that EMF drew are gone.

0.15.44 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: in the Drop button's tooltip, the warning about the game's "Auto-Collect Scattered Loot" setting is in red.

0.15.43 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: Auto, Dump Junk and Drop / Delete (and the two choices under Drop) explain themselves when you hover them.

0.15.42 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's windows use the game's mouse pointer again: a Windows resize pointer the game showed for a moment is no longer taken for it.

0.15.41 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's window (F6) stays open when you click another program or Alt+Tab; F6, Esc or its x close it.
- The Messages window stays on screen all the time in a world: the last 5 messages, the last 10 while the pointer is out.

0.15.40 Nov 13, 2026

0.15.39 Nov 13, 2026

- The party window hides while one of the game's menus is open (bag, map, skills, ...), like the minimap.

0.15.38 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: the option buttons are called Exclude Action Bar, Dump Key and Show All Bag Items, and hovering one explains it.

0.15.37 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: trophies (the heads bosses leave) are never junk and are no longer offered in the bag list.
- Auto Junk List: new button Show all bag items (off by default). On, every item in your bag is offered and can be junked, also weapons, armour, rings, tools, summoning items, trophies and high level gear. Off, those are never removed, even if one is on your junk list (client and server).
- The item tooltip no longer shows how many you carry: the number is on the item itself.

0.15.36 Nov 13, 2026
- Hovering an item in the Auto Junk List shows its details again: the name in its rarity's colour, item level, rarity, type, how many you carry, its name for chat commands, and what a click does.
- Item tiles are now a standard part of FlameKit's window: every feature that shows Enshrouded items shows them the same way, with the same tooltip.

0.15.34 Nov 13, 2026

It stays where you let go; "Back to its corner" in the Minimap tab puts it back. The "Move the minimap" button and its setting are gone.
- The minimap no longer hides while FlameKit's window is open or the pointer key is held.

0.15.33 Nov 13, 2026
- Auto Junk List: an item moved straight back (you changed your mind) has no gold frame any more; it is back where it was.

0.15.32 Nov 13, 2026

0.15.31 Nov 13, 2026
- Long lines in FlameKit's windows wrap to the next line instead of being cut off (in a window wider than its first size, for example the What's New tab).

0.15.30 Nov 13, 2026
- After an update, FlameKit's window opens by itself on the What's New tab, once, the first time you are in a world. What's New is also the tab the window opens on the first time in a game.
- New setting (Settings tab): open FlameKit's window every time you enter a world (off unless you switch it on).
- Auto Junk List: an item you just moved gets a gold frame, and the list it moved to shows the page it is on, so you can see what you just moved. In both directions (to the junk list and back to the bag). The frames go when the window closes.

0.15.29 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's window: What's New is the first tab. The Party tab is gone; its test players are in a new Debug section at the bottom of the Experimental tab, with FlameKit's log level (Off, Normal, Full; Ctrl+Shift+F12 still works) and where the logs are.
- Each feature's settings are in its own tab only: the minimap's corner, distance from the edge and keys are in the Minimap tab; the Auto Junk List's "never touch the action bar" switch and its dump key are buttons on its tab. The Settings tab keeps FlameKit's own settings and the switches that turn a feature on or off (a feature switched off has no tab).

0.15.28 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's window (F6) looks like the pinned windows: a title bar with FlameKit's version and an x that closes it, and a frame. Drag it by the title bar, and resize it from its lower right corner; it opens where and as big as you left it (the Windows tab can put it back in the middle).
- The Auto Junk List's icon grids fit the window's size: more icons across and more rows when the window is bigger.
- The tabs no longer run off the window: narrower tabs, and a second row when they still do not fit. The tabs are now Auto Junk List, Minimap, Experimental, Party, Settings, What's New, Windows.
- "Check for updates" moved into the What's New tab.
- Pinned windows (Party, Messages) can also be made shorter: their content then scrolls with the mouse wheel while the pointer key is held.
- Party window: the gold frame around the followed player sits one pixel under the mana bar instead of on it.

0.15.27 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's window (F6): long tabs (Settings, Minimap, Experimental, Party, What's New) scroll instead of showing pages: with the mouse wheel, or the scroll bar at the right (drag it, or click above or below it).

0.15.26 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's window (F6) has a Settings tab with every FlameKit setting: switches, choices, sizes with - and +, and keys (Change, then press the new key). They are the same settings as in EMF's Mods tab.
- The old FlameKit panel that EMF drew (F4) is gone: everything is in FlameKit's own window. Its key is a setting now (Key that opens FlameKit's window, F6).
- The pointer key for the pinned windows is a setting: Right Alt (as before), Right Ctrl or Caps Lock.
- A Messages window (pinned, top left): what FlameKit just did, for example "Junk discarded: Twigs x3", shows for 12 seconds; hold the pointer key to see the last 10. Warnings that EMF used to show at the top of the screen are there too. It can be moved, resized, collapsed or hidden like the party window.
- After an update, a message says so; what is new is in the What's New tab of FlameKit's window (instead of a window that opened by itself).
- Party window: a player with 0 health is marked DOWN in red, and has a red ring on the minimap.
- Party window: hold the pointer key and click a player to follow them on the minimap (a gold ring, and their name even at the minimap's edge); click them again to stop.

0.15.25 Nov 13, 2026
- The party window shows where each player is, under their name: the region, and for the other players how far away and in which direction from you (for example "Revelwood · 320 m NE"). For you it shows the region and the named place you are in or near, the same as under the minimap (client and server).

0.15.24 Nov 13, 2026
- When you hold Right Alt (or open FlameKit's window), the mouse pointer appears where it was the last time, instead of somewhere else each time; the first time, in the middle of the screen (client).

0.15.23 Nov 13, 2026
- For FlameKit's development: the server saves the world at once when FlameKit's restart helper asks for it, before a restart of the local dedicated server (server). Nothing changes in the game.

0.15.22 Nov 13, 2026
- Test players, for trying the party window and the minimap alone: FlameKit's window (F6), tab Party, buttons Off, 1, 3 and 6. The server makes them up and sends them to you the same way as real players (only you see them; it needs FlameKit on the server). They walk around you, some near and some far away at the minimap's edge, with health and mana that go up and down; Test Dain is down (0 health) for 4 seconds every 20 seconds. A server restart forgets them; your game asks again within 10 seconds.

0.15.21 Nov 13, 2026
- A party window, pinned on the screen while you play (client): every player in the game, you first, each with their level, a green health bar and a blue mana bar with the exact numbers. Each player's name has its own colour and symbol, the same as on the minimap.
- Hold Right Alt while playing to get the mouse pointer: then the party window can be dragged by its title bar, made wider or narrower from its lower right corner, collapsed (–) or hidden (×). Let go of Right Alt to play on. Where it is and how it looks is kept for the next game.
- FlameKit's window (F6) has a Windows tab: show or hide each pinned window, or put it back in its first place. It also shows the log level key (Ctrl+Shift+F12) and where the logs are.
- The minimap marks other players with their own symbol and colour instead of a white dot.
- On a server without FlameKit: an orange line under the FlameKit label says some features are off; the party window then shows only you and your health, and says what is missing.

0.15.20 Nov 13, 2026
- Updates arrive without GitHub's cache delay: the updater first asks GitHub for the newest commit and then downloads the files at that exact commit (client). Before, GitHub could hand out an old update list for up to 5 minutes after a new version.
- The test channel checks for updates every minute; players' games still check every 10 minutes.
- A "Check for updates" button in FlameKit's window (F6) checks at once; the lower left corner then says "FlameKit is up to date" for a few seconds, or shows the green "ready" line.
- FlameKit's log: a repeated "up to date" check is a detail (full level only); failed checks are warnings.

0.15.19 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's window (F6, client) has tabs: Auto Junk List, Minimap and Experimental. The Minimap and Experimental tabs have the same buttons as in the old panel and do the same things; any feature with a tab shows up there.
- Long tabs show in pages (< 1/2 >) instead of scrolling. Hovering a button shows its explanation.
- While FlameKit's window is open the mouse pointer shows over the whole game window, not only over FlameKit's window; a click outside FlameKit's window does nothing.
- FlameKit's windows use the game's own mouse pointer once the game has shown it (in the bag, the map or any menu); until then Windows' arrow.
- The client writes the tabs and the rows of the tab shown into ui_tabs.dat for FlameKit's window; clicks come back through ui_actions.txt.
- Tests: the tab bridge (rows written only while the tab is shown, a click does what the panel's button does, a click for rows no longer shown is dropped).

0.15.18 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's log (client) no longer records other programs' window titles: a window that is not the game's is logged only by its program's file name (e.g. notepad.exe) and window class.
- FlameKit's log never contains the Windows user name: it is written as <user> (it appears in folder paths).

0.15.17 Nov 13, 2026
- A new version no longer changes anything in a running game: the updater downloads it, holds FlameKit's Lua part in emf\flamekit_update until the next game start and puts it in place then, so FlameKit's label keeps showing the version you are running until you restart (client).
- The update line in the lower left corner is green when an update is ready and says "Update v... is ready: restart the game"; red when an update failed, orange while downloading.

0.15.16 Nov 13, 2026
- FlameKit's UI (client) is drawn in one overlay window instead of three: the minimap, the Auto Junk List window (F6) and the lines in the lower left corner are layers of one picture. The picture is plain memory, so it can later be drawn inside the game's own frame (Vulkan) instead.
- The overlay counts as "in front" whenever any window of the game is the front window (it went missing after Alt+Tab), and Windows now tells FlameKit at once when the front window changes.
- A watchdog checks 4 times a second that the overlay is shown and in front of the game; every failure is logged with the window that was in the way, and repaired.
- FlameKit's own log (client): emf\mods\flamekit\logs\flamekit_<date>_<time>.log, one per game session, the newest 10 kept, up to 50 MB each. It has FlameKit's DLL, EMF's log (with the Lua part's lines), Windows and screen details, the game's memory and CPU use, the updater, the UI and the watchdog.
- Debug level in emf\mods\flamekit\debug.txt: off, normal (the default) or full; changes while the game runs. Ctrl+Shift+F12 in the game steps through the levels. Errors and warnings are always logged. The level shows in the lower left corner when it is not normal.
- The updater logs every check (up to date, failed and why), not only downloads.
- The Lua part (client and server) logs at the debug level too: clicks from FlameKit's window, the junk list going to the server half, files written for the DLL.
- A crash in one of FlameKit's own threads is logged with where it happened.
- Tests: the debug level is read from debug.txt, and off writes only warnings and errors.

0.15.15 Nov 13, 2026
- Fix: the lines in the lower left corner (FlameKit label, update line, status line) were hidden behind the game (client); they now stay in front of it, as the minimap does.
- The client log says when those lines show or hide, where and why.

0.15.14 Nov 13, 2026
- The lines in the lower left corner (client) are drawn by FlameKit itself, no longer by EMF: the status line on top, then the FlameKit label, then the update line.

- Tests: the lower-left lines are checked in ui_hud.dat, and no line may be drawn by EMF.

- New buttons in that window: Auto (ON: junk is removed as you loot it), Dump Junk, and a Drop/Delete list. They change the same settings as the panel's buttons.

0.15.12 Nov 13, 2026

- Changes made in that window are the same as in the panel: saved to your list and sent to the server.
